reason: The picture shows recycling cells breaking down worn red cells, which should help recover their iron.
expectation: The recycling cells will break down the worn cells and make their iron available for reuse.

effect: The worn cells yielded iron carried in blood, ready to be reused.
reaction: It is satisfying to see part of an old cell reused rather than discarded.
reason: The goal calls for using recovered iron in new red cells, and the marrow contains developing blood cells and their other nutrients.

choice.combine: Iron recovered from old blood cells

expectation: The marrow will use the recovered iron to help make new red blood cells.

effect: The recovered iron is now in the oxygen-carrying protein of new red cells; the skin-cell goal remains.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the iron reused while the marrow remains intact.
reason: The picture shows water, glucose and building materials moving toward the dividing skin cells, matching the remaining goal.

choice.combine: Dividing cells at the skin's base
choice.with: Water, glucose and cell building materials

expectation: The supplied materials will help the skin's base cells grow replacement cells.

effect: The new skin cells formed above the intact base population while older surface cells shed, completing the remaining goal.
reaction: It was satisfying to see how the skin stays covered while its cells are replaced.

mostWorthwhile.text: Reusing recovered iron in marrow was most worthwhile because it connected worn-out red cells to the oxygen-carrying protein in new ones.

leastWorthwhile.text: Supplying materials to the skin cells was straightforward and less interesting as a decision, though the result clearly showed renewal.

surprise.text: I was surprised that iron from old red cells could be reused in new cells while the marrow's stem cells remained.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary; the pictures and goals explained the pairings.

continue.text: I would probably continue to see more connections between body systems, although these particular pairings were quite predictable.
